Holzbaurechner / Deck joist span

Deck joist span calculator

Which joist size do you need, how big must the beam be and how far apart can the posts go? The calculator applies the deck span tables of the 2021 International Residential Code and lists the framing lumber.

Joist spans in the 2021 IRC

Table R507.6 lists how far a deck joist may span between supports, depending on species, size and spacing. These are the values for No. 2 lumber, 40 psf live load and 10 psf dead load:

Joist12 in. o.c.16 in. o.c.24 in. o.c.
Southern pine
2x69' 11"9' 0"7' 7"
2x813' 1"11' 10"9' 8"
2x1016' 2"14' 0"11' 5"
2x1218' 0"16' 6"13' 6"
Douglas fir-larch, hem-fir, spruce-pine-fir
2x69' 6"8' 8"7' 2"
2x812' 6"11' 1"9' 1"
2x1015' 8"13' 7"11' 1"
2x1218' 0"15' 9"12' 10"
Redwood, western cedars, ponderosa pine, red pine
2x68' 10"8' 0"6' 10"
2x811' 8"10' 7"8' 8"
2x1014' 11"13' 0"10' 7"
2x1217' 5"15' 1"12' 4"

The span is measured from the face of the ledger or beam to the face of the next support. Joists may overhang a beam by up to a quarter of their span, within the cantilever limits of the same table. The calculator keeps the overhang at no more than 2 ft.

How the beam is sized

A dropped beam carries the joists and sits on posts. Table R507.5 gives the allowed distance between posts for each built-up beam, depending on how much deck the beam carries. The more joist span on the beam, the closer the posts must be. The calculator compares two- and three-ply beams of 2x8, 2x10 and 2x12 with different post counts and picks the cheapest combination. A beam may overhang its end posts by up to a quarter of the post spacing.

Built-up beams need their plies fastened together with two rows of nails or screws, and splices may only fall over a post.

Spacing and decking

The joist spacing is limited by the deck boards, not only by the joists: 5/4 wood boards and most composite boards allow 16 in. on center, 2x6 decking allows 24 in. Diagonal decking needs closer spacing. If you plan composite boards, the manufacturer's installation guide decides.

Frequently asked questions

What size joists do I need for a 12 ft span?
For a 12 ft span at 16 in. on center you need 2x10 joists in southern pine, Douglas fir or hem-fir. A 2x8 reaches 11 ft 10 in. at the most. At 12 in. on center a southern pine 2x8 would be enough (13 ft 1 in.).
How far apart can deck posts be?
That depends on the beam and on the joist span it carries. A double 2x10 southern pine beam under joists spanning 12 ft allows posts about 7 ft 4 in. apart, a triple 2x12 about 10 ft 9 in.
Can I use 4x4 posts for a deck?
The IRC still allows 4x4 posts for low decks, but 6x6 posts are the standard. They are stiffer, give room for a notched beam seat and are what most building departments expect. The calculator always uses 6x6 posts.
Does the deck need blocking between joists?
The IRC requires the joist ends to be restrained against rolling, by a rim joist, blocking or hurricane ties. Mid-span blocking is not required but stiffens longer joists, so the calculator adds a row on spans over 8 ft.

Lumber sizes follow the span tables of the 2021 International Residential Code (IRC) and are planning values. They do not replace a permit review or an engineer. Decks, patio covers and carports usually need a building permit, so check with your local building department.
